full_inspection: All four complete native halves of sites047 and123 were independently read and compared, including all margins and every formula. The enlarged audit_123_details.jpg checks the two overstrike layers, the copy1-only point after vu, the shared typed overlap in d’ailleurs and the isolated gray marginal trace. Remaining body text corresponds.
original_transcription_comparison: The supplied originals differ in the overwritten ti/ét and foliation47/123. They both center a widehat over M, while the images show an upper-right caret. Copy1’s original omission of the point after vu was already corrected; direct comparison confirms that copy2 lacks this point. The replacement ét in copy2 is now resolved, with explicit uncertainty retained for its covered lower layer.

entries.reason: Both native images show the same displaced caret and regular typed nu; copy2’s original centered widehat is corrected.

entries.decision: retain the clear handwritten replacement and the doubtful lower layer as a copy2 variant
entries.reason: The manuscript acute/e/t strokes clearly read ét. They cover much of the typed ti, which is corroborated by the clear paired copy1 word but remains uncertain beneath the overstrike.
The small point after vu is present in copy1 and absent in copy2. The category records a body-reading difference without deciding the point’s origin.

entries.decision: record the observed point-shaped trace without assigning textual role or hand
entries.reason: An isolated gray point-shaped trace appears in copy2’s left margin beside dant par. Its visible shape is retained as a doubtful margin mark in the diplomatic source and apparatus; its origin and textual role remain unresolved, without attribution to handwriting.
The lower-left inscriptions read47 and123; no authorship attribution is made.
